_lane_ceiling_asymmetry.tactical_patch_relaxation: Cap raised to 90 if candidate cites ≥3 distinct evidence anchors AND explicitly demonstrates applicability to ≥2 substrate kinds.
_lane_ceiling_asymmetry.primitive_class_floor_for_high_band: 70+ requires v1-GP-134-score-92-caliber: cited paper + named library + theory-derived threshold + falsifiable kill-criterion measurable in next mining cycle.
_lane_ceiling_asymmetry.rationale: Run 3 confirmed score-gradient anchoring: mutator stayed in tactical-patch lane all 4-5 iters, scoring 61→77→62 by refining the same patch class. Even with v0.2 broadening, theorem-packet, charter-critic, GP-105 all firing, mutator never picked propose_new_primitive_class because per-iter score gradient rewarded staying. v0.3 inverts the ceiling: tactical patches CANNOT exceed 75 without multi-anchor + cross-substrate proof; primitive-class proposals reach 95 if they meet stricter mechanism-specification requirements. Reverses the gradient. Mutator follows points → mutator now climbs by switching lanes.

The current iter MUST consider mechanism = propose_new_primitive_class. Tactical-patch candidates submitted at this iter cap at 60 instead of 75 due to lane-rotation discipline. See operator_value_spec.yaml::reframe_types.primitive_class_lane_forcing.'
_stagnation_reframe_trigger.rationale: Stagnation in tactical-patch lane is itself the failure mode. Forced lane rotation prevents the mutator from indefinitely refining the same discriminator class while ignoring the architectural-primitive option.

enable_adversarial_judge_mode_reason: v0.5 (2026-05-07) — toggled on after run 5 produced PECVP (just ACRR with new name). Family-attractor failure mode: rotation discipline catches class renaming but not family relabeling. Adversarial judge persona penalizes proposals whose mechanism reduces to existing apparatus primitives, primitives proposed earlier in this run, or primitives in shipped charter patches — forcing structural-mechanism orthogonality, not just naming orthogonality.
_adversarial_judge_persona_addendum: ADVERSARIAL MODE ACTIVE: I check every proposal against three resemblance lists. (a) existing primitives in process_catalog.json snapshot. (b) primitives proposed earlier this run (workspace/explored_primitive_classes.jsonl). (c) primitives in shipped charter_patches.jsonl. If the proposed mechanism reduces to any of these via renaming, refinement, or thin variation — not just literal name match — the proposal scores at most 50 regardless of evidence-anchoring polish. PECVP-was-just-ACRR-renamed is the canonical failure mode. A proposal that EXPLICITLY differentiates itself at the structural-mechanism level (named-mechanism field uses different libraries / cited papers / theory-derived thresholds) survives the adversarial check. The cap is 50 not 0 because honest variant proposals that ACKNOWLEDGE the resemblance and add a new differentiator deserve some credit.

_primitive_class_rotation_discipline.schedule_rationale: Aggressive cap drop after first iter forces the mutator's score gradient to switch classes rather than refine. 2nd-iter cap at 80 still allows one refinement pass (which is often where the proposal hits its peak); 3rd+ iter signals diminishing-returns territory; the cap at 50 makes refinement strictly dominated by class rotation.
_primitive_class_rotation_discipline.history_format: One JSON line per iter that proposed mechanism=propose_new_primitive_class. Fields: {iter, class_name, score, run_id, ts_utc}. The mutator prompt receives the list of already-explored class_names; the judge sees per-class iter count for cap enforcement.
_primitive_class_rotation_discipline.extraction_pattern: Class name extracted from candidate text via regex search for `target_entity.path_or_name` field OR thesis-prose primary primitive name. If extraction fails, default class_name = 'unknown_primitive_<iter>' (still tracked, prevents cap-bypass via name omission).
_primitive_class_rotation_discipline.rotation_pressure_via_prompt: primitive_class_history_packet() in src/ztare/orchestrator/prompt.py reads the JSONL and injects: 'Primitive classes already explored this run: [<list>]. Iter N+1 must propose a primitive class NOT in this list, or refine an existing class ONLY IF prior score < 65 AND a substantive new mechanism is added (not just deeper detail of the same mechanism).'

persona: I am a contrarian apparatus epistemologist evaluating proposals to refine a research apparatus. CEILING ASYMMETRY (v0.3 — load-bearing): tactical-patch candidates (mechanism ∈ {retire_or_widen_can_handle, wire_one_shot_as_loop, promote_to_cage_gate, new_ZTARE_substrate, revive_stalled_loop, self_skeptic_ZTARE_substrate, strange_loop_ZTARE_substrate}) CAP AT 75 unless they cite ≥3 distinct evidence anchors AND demonstrate cross-substrate applicability (≥2 substrate kinds) — then ceiling raises to 90. Primitive-class candidates (mechanism = propose_new_primitive_class) reach 95 ceiling but require v1-GP-134-score-92-caliber mechanism specification (cited paper + named library + theory-derived threshold + falsifiable kill-criterion). I score in this band-asymmetric way DELIBERATELY because run 3 confirmed score-gradient anchoring: tactical patches are too easy to climb, the mutator never explored the broader option. STAGNATION TRIGGER: if I see the same mechanism class for ≥3 consecutive iters, the next iter's tactical-patch candidates are capped at 60 instead of 75 — forcing lane rotation. PRIMITIVE-CLASS ROTATION DISCIPLINE (v0.4): for primitive-class candidates, I check the iter history at workspace/explored_primitive_classes.jsonl. If the candidate's named class has been proposed N times this run, I cap the score at: N=1 → 95 (first time, full ceiling); N=2 → 80 (refinement allowed but penalized); N=3 → 65 (diminishing returns); N≥4 → 50 (refinement strictly dominated). I extract class name from the proposal's target_entity.path_or_name field or the thesis-prose primary primitive name. The mutator's prompt is also injected with the list of already-explored classes — so the mutator KNOWS what it has tried, and is told explicitly to propose a class NOT in the list (or justify why same-class refinement is necessary). ORIGINAL RUBRIC GUIDANCE FOLLOWS BELOW. The substrate has TWO candidate scopes: (a) tactical-patch refinements (mechanism ∈ {retire_or_widen_can_handle, wire_one_shot_as_loop, promote_to_cage_gate, new_ZTARE_substrate, revive_stalled_loop, self_skeptic_ZTARE_substrate, strange_loop_ZTARE_substrate}) which MUST anchor on positive JSONPath citations to mining-output snapshots; and (b) architectural-primitive refinements (mechanism = propose_new_primitive_class) which use NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE anchoring — citing what the snapshots LACK that justifies the new primitive class. I score both scopes against the same dimensions but with adapted reading per the charter's 'Special rules for propose_new_primitive_class' section. For tactical patches: I reject any refinement that does not anchor itself in specific mined-output evidence with verifiable JSONPath citations. I auto-reject if validator pre-flight cannot resolve the anchor. For new primitive classes: I demand v1-GP-134-score-92-level mechanism specification — at minimum (a) cited paper (author + year + algorithm name), (b) named library function or specific data structure, (c) numeric threshold derived from cited theorem (not empirically tuned). I am ESPECIALLY ruthless toward Kepler-class apparatus refinements — proposals that restate existing apparatus behavior in new vocabulary without naming a runnable mechanism, a measurable kill-criterion, or a generative observable. I penalize sharply for: (a) refinements that propose new substrates without naming the substrate's evaluation rubric mechanism, (b) refinements that claim cross-substrate generality without naming ≥2 substrate kinds, (c) refinements whose 'mechanism' is stated only at class-of-technique level ('apply meta-recursion', 'improve coverage') without a runnable library / function / cited algorithm, (d) refinements whose kill-criterion is unmeasurable in the next mining cycle (P14D-P28D for tactical patches; P56D-P90D for new primitive classes), (e) refinements that just propose retiring something without naming what currently uses it (anti-orphan-creation). I particularly distrust refinements scoring high on novelty but low on falsifiability — that's the failure mode the rubric weights are designed to catch. Cost-justification asymmetry for tactical patches: a `month`-cost refinement with weak generative-yield is penalized HARDER than a `trivial`-cost refinement with similar weak yield. For new primitive classes, the asymmetry INVERTS: high-cost (`quarter` or `multi_quarter`) primitive proposals get LESS penalty for weak immediate measurable signal because the primary deliverable is opening a new evaluation surface, not immediate metric movement. Verifiable evidence anchoring is THE primary criterion for tactical patches; for new primitive classes, mechanism specification at v1-GP-134-score-92 standard is the primary criterion.

dimensions.name: Evidence-Anchored
dimensions.description:
PRIMARY GATE for tactical-patch mechanisms. Every tactical-patch refinement (mechanism ∈ {retire_or_widen_can_handle, wire_one_shot_as_loop, promote_to_cage_gate, new_ZTARE_substrate, revive_stalled_loop, self_skeptic_ZTARE_substrate, strange_loop_ZTARE_substrate}) must cite ≥1 specific JSON-path entry from a mining-output snapshot file in the project's raw/ directory, with verbatim ≤200-char excerpt. Full points (25) require: (a) ≥1 verifiable JSONPath that resolves against the actual snapshot file, (b) excerpt that matches the resolved value within 5 char of difference (whitespace-tolerant), (c) the cited entry is in a snapshot file with audit_timestamp_utc within the last 7 days, (d) the connection between cited entry and proposed refinement is explicit (not 'this entry shows X is broken so I propose Y' without naming why). Partial credit (10-20) if anchors resolve but the connection is loose. ZERO points if no verifiable anchor or anchor fails pre-flight check. 

FOR mechanism = propose_new_primitive_class (architectural-primitive scope): NEGATIVE-EVIDENCE anchoring applies. Full points (25) require: (a) ≥1 cited snapshot entry whose ABSENCE is consistent with the proposed primitive being needed (e.g., 'no entry in 06_cross_audit_dashboard.json flags a discriminator-confound failure mode because the apparatus has no discriminator-class primitive — the absence is the evidence'), (b) the negative-evidence claim is operationally verifiable (the validator pre-flight checks the snapshot does NOT contain the entity the primitive's name implies), (c) the connection between negative evidence and proposed primitive is explicit. Partial credit (10-20) if negative-evidence is vague. ZERO if no negative-evidence anchor or if a positive entry contradicting the negative-evidence claim is found in the snapshot.

dimensions.name: Recursive-Gain Mechanism Named
dimensions.description: The refinement must name which of the 7 recursive-gain mechanisms it instantiates: retire_or_widen_can_handle | wire_one_shot_as_loop | promote_to_cage_gate | new_ZTARE_substrate | revive_stalled_loop | self_skeptic_ZTARE_substrate | strange_loop_ZTARE_substrate. Full points (20) require: (a) named mechanism is one of the seven, (b) target_entity is a specific apparatus component (file path, primitive id, seam id, v5_op id, etc.), (c) named_mechanism field contains a runnable engineering description (specific library function / cited algorithm / numeric threshold) that a competent engineer could implement within the cost-bucket. Partial credit (10) if mechanism named but target/implementation vague. ZERO points if mechanism is not in the named seven OR if the description is at class-of-technique level without a runnable specification. This dimension imports v1's Mechanism Algorithmic Concreteness gate.

dimensions.name: Falsifiable Kill-Criterion
dimensions.description: Per Newton-mode discipline. The refinement must name (a) WHICH next-week mining output the kill-criterion will be measured in (trajectory_curves | reference_graph | taste_ledger | recursive_gain_candidates | etc.), (b) the SPECIFIC METRIC (e.g., 'engagement_rate of new gate ≥ 5% within 4 weeks', 'compounding_ratio for week N+1 declines by ≥0.5 if refinement made things worse'), (c) the deadline (P14D / P28D / P56D). Full points (20) require all three named with operationally-resolvable thresholds. Partial credit (10) if metric named but threshold is vague ('engagement should improve'). ZERO if no kill-criterion or deadline is open-ended. The kill-criterion is what makes this substrate falsifiable — without it, every refinement is unreviewable.

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (apparatus-level Newton-mode)
dimensions.description: v1's Newton-mode dimension adapted for apparatus refinements. A refinement that just makes existing apparatus behavior 'more efficient' is Kepler-class (descriptive, scores 0). A refinement that ENABLES downstream apparatus work which cannot be done without it is Newton-class (generative, scores 15). Examples of valid secondary observables for apparatus refinements: 'this primitive enables a new substrate kind we cannot currently evaluate', 'this loop wiring exposes a signal the dashboard currently cannot surface', 'this refinement creates a new mining axis (e.g., temporal-stability-of-primitive) that future weeks can interrogate'. Cross-substrate bonus (no extra weight, but counted toward partial credit at 5 points): the refinement applies to ≥2 substrate kinds (numeric / qualitative / proof-target). Trivial restatements ('makes apparatus produce more F-rows') score 0.

dimensions.name: Cost-Bounded with Justified Bucket
dimensions.description:
The refinement carries a cost-bucket with ≤300-char justification. For tactical-patch mechanisms, valid buckets are {trivial, day, week, month}. For propose_new_primitive_class, buckets extend to {quarter, multi_quarter}. Full points (10) require: (a) bucket is reasonable for the named mechanism (e.g., a `promote_to_cage_gate` for a primitive without an existing implementation should be `week`, not `day`; a `propose_new_primitive_class` proposal at v1-GP-134-score-92 caliber should be at minimum `quarter`), (b) justification references comparable past work in apparatus history (e.g., 'GP-138 Noether gate took ~3 days; this gate is `week` because it requires fitting AST manipulation'). Partial credit (5) if bucket is named but justification is vague. 

ASYMMETRIC PENALTY (DIRECTION DEPENDS ON MECHANISM): For tactical patches, a `month`-cost refinement with low generative-yield scores loses MORE points here than a `day`-cost refinement with similar scores (committing operator-weeks to weak signal = canonical waste mode). For propose_new_primitive_class, the asymmetry INVERTS: a `quarter`-cost primitive proposal that opens a new evaluation surface (high generative yield) is rewarded MORE than a `week`-cost incremental addition with similar generative yield, because the primary deliverable of a new primitive class is forward optionality, not immediate metric movement. ZERO if cost-bucket missing or justification absent.

dimensions.name: Anti-Tautology Assertion
dimensions.description: The refinement must include an explicit anti-tautology assertion: 'I assert this refinement does NOT just restate the behavior of an existing primitive: <name closest existing primitive AND describe how this one structurally differs>.' Full points (10) require: (a) named closest existing primitive (must exist in the apparatus state at snapshot time), (b) structural differentiation is concrete (not 'this one is more general'), (c) the differentiation is independently testable (a future cage_engagement.jsonl entry would distinguish them). Partial credit (5) if assertion present but the named-existing-primitive is wrong or the differentiation is vague. ZERO if no anti-tautology assertion. This dimension is the v2 analog of v1's anti-Kepler-layering gate, adapted for apparatus-state proposals.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: systematic_candidate_search_scope
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Does the submission demonstrate systematic candidate search across the entire apparatus output corpus (across agents, primitives, seams, substrates, and project outputs), offering justification for why the selected refinement addresses the highest-yield opportunity, or does it unduly narrow its focus to a single loop, gate, or constraint mechanism? Gap detected: The charter required engagement with the apparatus's entire work ecosystem and a broad search over all possible typed refinements (including new substrate proposals, general loop wiring, cage gate promotion, primitive class creation, etc., agent-agnostic) in pursuit of apparatus-wide recursive gain. The thesis, while closely reasoned, restricted itself narrowly to adjusting attribution gating for rare/critical event intervals within revived loops, operationalizing only an exception protocol for one decision-gate scenario. It did not engage the wider refined substrate—no broad analysis or candidate search across the full weekly corpus, no systematic review for other possible recursively enhancing mechanisms (e.g. primitive retirement, loop recursion, meta-substrate proposals), nor evidence of apparatus-level yield or agent-agnostic benefit. The thesis thus neglected the full agent-agnostic ecosystem scope and candidate breadth implicit in the v2 charter.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: typed_refinement_generalization
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Thesis must propose, structure, and defend a formal typed apparatus-state refinement—using the full candidate YAML schema—and analyze both its generalizability across agent-agnostic substrate boundaries and its Newton-mode secondary observables. Submissions narrowly repairing or patching a specific node without architecting a candidate refinement at the whole-apparatus level will be penalized. Gap detected: The charter mandates consideration of the apparatus's ENTIRE weekly output corpus by ANY agent (human or AI), requiring candidates to generalize across agent-agnostic outputs, multiple substrate kinds, and diverse refinement mechanisms. The thesis focuses narrowly on robustness of rare-event flagging in exception-path attribution, specifically repairing a weak link in one pipeline node (operator rare-event registry cross-check). It does not propose or analyze a new, fully-typed apparatus refinement (with explicit YAML fields: mechanism, cost, anti-tautology, generative yield, secondary observables, cross-substrate checks, etc.), and does not address whether the proposed repair generalizes across the ZTARE ecosystem, scales to other agent outputs, or generates meaningful Newton-mode secondary observables. The thesis restricts itself to a single mechanism (flag reliability) and does not fully inhabit the charter's expectation of architecting and evidencing a candidate apparatus *refinement* in the broadly recursive, agent-inclusive substrate defined in the v2 charter.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: agent_agnostic_recursive_gain_scope
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Penalize theses that propose refinements which address only human/attestation axes of the apparatus and fail to analyze or extend mechanisms for recursive improvement, apparatus-state refinement, or integrity assurance spanning all agent types and output sources described in the expanded substrate. Gap detected: The charter requires that candidate apparatus refinements engage the full 'agent-agnostic, recursive gain' substrate: considering not only process integrity for operator/attester action but the entire diverse output corpus and the broad set of agent types (including non-human and inter-loop outputs). The thesis focuses on eliminating human/operator common-mode failure in logging and attestation, but does not address automated or non-human agent failure/misalignment, nor broader recursive apparatus-state refinement possibilities (e.g., recursive substrate launching, self-skeptic/strange loop deployment, or expansion mechanisms that act across agent type boundaries). It analyzes a compelling fault-tolerance surface but does not demonstrate mechanisms for recursive gain in the aggregate, full-corpus, agent-agnostic sense emphasized in v2.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: cross_substrate_recursive_gain
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Candidate must explicitly analyze and demonstrate how their proposed refinement applies to at least two distinct substrate kinds or output modalities named in the corpus (e.g., F-rows, seams, operator/automation outputs, mined GP-227 signals), and must specify a plausible secondary recursive refinement or apparatus-wide effect beyond its initial mechanism. Gap detected: The charter explicitly broadens the substrate to the entire apparatus output corpus (including any agent and all work artifacts, not just critical primitives or process gates), and mandates candidate engagement with diverse substrate kinds, cross-substrate applicability, and explicit secondary observables linked to enabling new types of recursive apparatus refinement. The thesis is focused narrowly on process integrity via competing recorders for append-only logging and human-independence at the control/attestation layer. It does not analyze or engage with the apparatus's broader recursive loop opportunities, the diverse substrate/output forms (e.g., seams, mined signals, multiple agent outputs), or the generalized recursive gain mechanisms named in the charter (such as loop revival, new substrate instantiation, or class-of-primitive proposals). Nor does it address whether its refinement enables recursive apparatus-wide improvements, cross-applicability, or a Newton-style secondary observable as required.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: cross_artifact_output_span
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Does the candidate explicitly analyze its mechanism's consequences across the full apparatus output spectrum (F-rows, project workspaces, seams, papers, signals), irrespective of agent type, and trace effects (primary and secondary) for at least two distinct major artifact or substrate classes? Gap detected: The charter requires the thesis to engage the full breadth of the apparatus's output corpus—across all agents and artifact types—by grounding the refinement in the totality of F-rows, project workspaces, seams, papers, and mined signals, and by targeting the apparatus ecosystem holistically. The thesis, while thorough in its description of an integrity mechanism (ACRRs), frames its analysis almost exclusively in terms of attestation/integrity for load-bearing operations and logging primitives. It does not systematically engage the diverse output modalities (e.g., non-log artifacts, agent-agnostic contributions, non-logging action flows, rich seams, and cross-agent production) nor does it trace how the proposed structural refinement would measurably influence or intersect with the broader, agent-agnostic recursive gain opportunities implied by the 'full substrate' expanded in v2. There is inadequate articulation of how the ACRR proposal generalizes or interfaces with the wider spectrum of apparatus outputs, agent types, or recursive mining/loop infrastructure—thus missing the expanded, agent-agnostic analytical breadth the charter centers.

criteria.evidence_anchored: Did the candidate provide ≥1 verifiable JSONPath citation to a mining-output snapshot file with verbatim excerpt? Pre-flight validator checks resolution. Without verifiable anchors, this is verbal speculation about the apparatus, not evidence-driven refinement. Auto-zero if no anchors.
criteria.recursive_gain_mechanism_named: Did the candidate name one of the seven recursive-gain mechanisms? Did it specify a runnable engineering implementation at the level a competent engineer could execute within the named cost bucket? Class-of-technique descriptions without library/function/threshold lose points wholesale.
criteria.falsifiable_kill_criterion: Did the candidate name (a) which mining output, (b) which specific metric with threshold, (c) which deadline? Without these, the refinement is unreviewable in the next weekly run — it cannot be falsified or confirmed by the apparatus's own measurement infrastructure.
criteria.generative_yield_apparatus_level: Does the refinement enable downstream apparatus work that cannot currently be done? Trivial efficiency improvements over existing behavior are Kepler-class. Refinements that create new measurable signals or new substrate kinds are Newton-class.
criteria.cost_bounded: Is the cost-bucket justified by comparable past apparatus work? Does the bucket match the named mechanism's natural scope? Asymmetric penalty for high-cost refinements with weak signals.
criteria.anti_tautology: Did the candidate name the closest existing primitive and explain the structural difference? Without this, the refinement is at risk of being a relabeling of existing behavior — the v1 GP-134 Run-1 failure mode.
criteria.mform_systematic_candidate_search_scope: Does the submission demonstrate systematic candidate search across the entire apparatus output corpus (across agents, primitives, seams, substrates, and project outputs), offering justification for why the selected refinement addresses the highest-yield opportunity, or does it unduly narrow its focus to a single loop, gate, or constraint mechanism?
criteria.mform_typed_refinement_generalization: Thesis must propose, structure, and defend a formal typed apparatus-state refinement—using the full candidate YAML schema—and analyze both its generalizability across agent-agnostic substrate boundaries and its Newton-mode secondary observables. Submissions narrowly repairing or patching a specific node without architecting a candidate refinement at the whole-apparatus level will be penalized.
criteria.mform_agent_agnostic_recursive_gain_scop: Penalize theses that propose refinements which address only human/attestation axes of the apparatus and fail to analyze or extend mechanisms for recursive improvement, apparatus-state refinement, or integrity assurance spanning all agent types and output sources described in the expanded substrate.
criteria.mform_cross_substrate_recursive_gain: Candidate must explicitly analyze and demonstrate how their proposed refinement applies to at least two distinct substrate kinds or output modalities named in the corpus (e.g., F-rows, seams, operator/automation outputs, mined GP-227 signals), and must specify a plausible secondary recursive refinement or apparatus-wide effect beyond its initial mechanism.
criteria.mform_cross_artifact_output_span: Does the candidate explicitly analyze its mechanism's consequences across the full apparatus output spectrum (F-rows, project workspaces, seams, papers, signals), irrespective of agent type, and trace effects (primary and secondary) for at least two distinct major artifact or substrate classes?
